stops.stop: Vienna, the palais on the Landstrasse: Bastien und Bastienne
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The commission and the work are attested; the staging in Mesmer's garden theatre rests on Georg Nikolaus Nissen's posthumous biography alone, with no contemporary programme, letter, or score annotation, and Nissen himself reported finding no proof. The commission is also claimed for Mesmer's cousin Joseph Conrad Mesmer. Earliest securely documented staging is Berlin, 1890. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from mesmer.journey.json.

stops.stop: Rome, the Sistine Chapel: the Miserere
stops.date_confidence: attested by Leopold's own letter written within days; the day given is the Holy Week date in standard chronologies. Later retellings inflate the papal secrecy and the claim of a single unaided hearing. The Golden Spur investiture in July is attested separately and is folded into this stop.

stops.stop: Bologna, the Accademia Filarmonica: the examination
stops.date_confidence: attested for the admission and for the summer study with Martini; the surviving exercise sheet showing correction in another hand is documented in the academy's own archive.

stops.stop: Milan, the Teatro Regio Ducale: Mitridate
stops.date_confidence: attested. The research pool placed this theatre near Piazza della Scala at 45.4676/9.1897, which is La Scala, a separate later building inaugurated in 1778. The Teatro Regio Ducale was a wing of the ducal palace beside the cathedral at 45.4632/9.19114 and burned on 25 February 1776; the corrected pin is used here.

The research pool's 48.2065/16.3663 matches neither. Joseph II's 'too many notes' remark reaches us only through Niemetschek's later biography and is tagged R.

stops.stop: Prague, the Estates Theatre: La clemenza di Tito
stops.date_confidence: attested. Flagged: an automated extraction of the Wikipedia article rendered this premiere as 6 December 1791, which is impossible, since Mozart is dead on 5 December. The coronation-opera date of 6 September 1791 is the well-documented one and is used here. Estates Theatre coordinate corrected as at the Don Giovanni stop.

stops.stop: Vienna, the Theater auf der Wieden: Die Zauberflote
stops.date_confidence: attested for the premiere date and for Mozart conducting early performances. Coordinate corrected to Wikipedia's 48.19778, 16.36611 for the Theater auf der Wieden; the research pool's figure sat about 120 m west. The casting of Josepha Hofer as the Queen of the Night and Schikaneder as Papageno is standard and was not confirmed from the fetched source.

stops.stop: Vienna: the little Masonic cantata
stops.date_confidence: attested as the last completed entry in his own thematic catalogue. That the Requiem is absent from the catalogue follows from the catalogue itself; the anonymous commission through an intermediary is attested.

stops.stop: Vienna, Rauhensteingasse: the death
stops.date_confidence: attested for the illness, the attending physicians, the hour of death, and the register diagnosis. The rehearsal of the Requiem at the bedside on 4 December and the reported deathbed words to Sophie Haibel are secondhand recollections set down years later and are tagged R.

stops.stop: Vienna, St Stephen's: the consecration of the coffin
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to the chapel. The Mozarteum has the coffin consecrated at St Stephen's on 6 December at about three in the afternoon and transported that evening; the identification of the Crucifix chapel comes from later accounts rather than a contemporary document. The storm and the turned-back mourners are nineteenth-century additions.

stops.stop: Vienna: the poisoning that did not happen
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to the legend, which is what it is. There is no autopsy, no toxicology, no witness, and no document supporting a poisoning; the dramatic tradition from Pushkin in 1830 through Rimsky-Korsakov to Shaffer and Forman is attested as reception history. The date orders the segment at Pushkin's play.
